intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution for the best chance of witnessing the aurora borealis. Expert guides track solar activity and cloud cover to maximize your viewing experience, often venturing to remote highland areas.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & South Iceland highlands, departing from Reykjavik

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and sulfur minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and a swim-up bar serving Icelandic refreshments. Book the Comfort package for the full experience including towel and one drink.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (sunset or after dark for a magical atmosphere)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits amid bubbling hot springs and small geysers in a stunning rural landscape. A truly local and intimate experience.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and cultural landmarks on a guided walking tour. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, and Icelandic hot dogs. Visit the iconic Hallgrimskirkja church, the colorful old harbor, and local artisan shops.
experiences.location: 101 Reykjavik city center & Old Harbor district

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike & Natural Pool
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's stunning rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Fjallabak Nature Reserve and reward yourself with a soak in a natural geothermal hot spring river. The hike offers surreal landscapes of obsidian lava fields, steaming vents, and vivid mineral-streaked mountains unlike anywhere else on Earth.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the budget-friendly Flybus shuttle (~3,000 ISK) to Reykjavík and check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Freshen up and settle in.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or skip
meals.lunch: Meal on the flight or airport snack
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport Subway or a vending machine snack before the shuttle — keep it under 1,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely a travel and arrival day. The Flybus runs late to match international arrivals. Pre-book your shuttle online to save time. January nights in Iceland are long and dark — perfect northern lights conditions if skies clear during the drive!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. After a late breakfast, take a short walk along the beachfront near the resort to breathe in the Arctic sea air and get oriented. Explore the immediate shoreline — January light is brief (sunrise ~11:00), so enjoy the golden-hour glow over the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into central Reykjavík by local bus (Strætó bus, ~490 ISK). Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church (exterior free, tower ~1,000 ISK). Walk down Skólavörðustígur street, browse local shops, and visit Harpa Concert Hall (free exterior and lobby). Stroll along the Old Harbour waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area. Check the Aurora forecast (vedur.is or the Aurora app) — if KP index is 3+ and skies are clear, head to a dark spot near the beachfront for northern lights viewing. The coast away from city lights is ideal.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort — pick up supplies from a nearby Bónus supermarket (Iceland's cheapest chain). Skyr yogurt, bread, and fruit ~500 ISK
meals.lunch: Reykjavík: Hlöllabátar (Icelandic hot dog chain) — a classic pylsur hot dog for ~600 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the resort or Bónus supermarket meal — pasta or soup ~800 ISK total

day_by_day.notes: January sunrise is around 11:00 and sunset around 15:30, giving only ~4.5 hours of daylight. Plan outdoor sightseeing tightly around these hours. Stock up at Bónus supermarket to save significantly on food costs throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget Golden Circle day tour (book in advance ~8,000–10,000 ISK for a group tour). First stop: Þingvellir National Park — walk the rift valley between the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates. Free entry to the park itself.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle: Visit the Geysir Geothermal Area and watch Strokkur erupt every 5–10 minutes (free entry). Then head to the majestic Gullfoss waterfall — walk to the viewing platforms (free entry). Marvel at the frozen or semi-frozen cascade in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavík/resort by ~18:00. Check aurora forecast and head to the dark beachfront if conditions are favorable. The Golden Circle area on the return drive can also offer excellent aurora viewing away from city lights.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort — oatmeal with banana ~300 ISK
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from Bónus to eat on the tour bus or at Geysir — sandwiches and snacks ~700 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort — rice and canned fish or soup ~900 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Book the Golden Circle group tour online in advance for the best budget rates. Reykjavik Excursions and Gray Line offer affordable options. Dress in extreme warm layers — January temperatures can be -5°C to 3°C with wind chill. Waterproof boots are essential at Gullfoss.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the famous Blue Lagoon geothermal spa. Book the Comfort package in advance (~9,500 ISK — the most affordable tier). Located near Keflavík, it's accessible by direct Blue Lagoon bus from Reykjavík (~3,500 ISK round trip). Soak in the milky-blue 38–40°C waters surrounded by lava fields.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying the Blue Lagoon — use the silica mud masks (included) and relax in the steam caves. The lagoon is magical in winter with snow-dusted lava rocks around you. Depart by mid-afternoon and return to the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover. Check aurora forecast — the Blue Lagoon area on the drive back can offer aurora views if skies clear. Spend the evening near the resort beachfront scanning the sky.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort before departure — skyr and bread ~400 ISK
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from Bónus for the Blue Lagoon trip — granola bars and fruit ~500 ISK (food inside the lagoon is expensive)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort — hearty lamb soup from a packet (~Bónus, ~600 ISK) to warm up after the spa day

day_by_day.notes: Book the Blue Lagoon well in advance — it sells out frequently, especially in winter. The Comfort package is the minimum recommended tier. Avoid bringing jewelry into the lagoon as the silica-rich water can damage it. Bring your own shampoo and conditioner.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula independently by renting a small car for the day (~5,000–7,000 ISK including fuel) or joining a budget group tour. Visit the Bridge Between Continents — a small footbridge spanning the Eurasian and North American plates (free). Explore the dramatic lava fields and coastal cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Gunnuhver Hot Springs on the Reykjanes Peninsula — a powerful geothermal area with boiling mud pools and roaring steam vents (free entry). Walk the marked trails carefully. Head to the Reykjanes Lighthouse at Valahnúkamöl for dramatic coastal scenery and basalt sea stacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. The Reykjanes Peninsula is one of Iceland's best aurora-viewing locations due to minimal light pollution. Spend the evening outdoors if the forecast is favorable — set an alarm for midnight checks.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort — eggs and toast ~400 ISK
meals.lunch: Pack Bónus sandwiches and snacks for the day trip ~700 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort — pasta with tuna and tomato sauce ~800 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Gunnuhver is an active and powerful geothermal area — stay on marked paths at all times. The area around the Reykjanes Peninsula is geologically very active (volcanic eruptions have occurred in recent years — check local advisories at safetravel.is before visiting).

day_by_day.morning: Take the Strætó bus into Reykjavík. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) — entry ~2,000 ISK, offering a deep dive into Icelandic history and Viking heritage. Spend 2 hours exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjavík City Library or the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — an underground museum built around a 10th-century Viking longhouse (~1,800 ISK). Walk through the colorful streets of the 101 Reykjavík district. Browse the flea market at Kolaportið (open weekends, ~free entry) if visiting on a Saturday or Sunday.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavík's budget-friendly food scene. Walk along Laugavegur street. Return to the resort by bus. Check aurora forecast for late-night viewing.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort — skyr with granola ~400 ISK
meals.lunch: Reykjavík: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — the most famous hot dog stand in Iceland, a must-try ~600 ISK
meals.dinner: Reykjavík: Hlemmur Mathöll food hall — various budget options from ~1,500–2,500 ISK. Try Icelandic fish and chips or a bowl of kjötsúpa (lamb soup)

day_by_day.notes: Kolaportið flea market is only open on weekends — a great place to find budget souvenirs and Icelandic snacks like hákarl (fermented shark). The Settlement Exhibition is one of Reykjavík's most unique museums and highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day / flexible morning. Sleep in or take a slow morning walk along the beachfront. Use the time to do laundry, repack, and plan the second half of the trip. Review aurora forecasts and upcoming weather.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local geothermal public swimming pool — Reykjavík has several (Laugardalslaug or Nauthólsvík geothermal beach if accessible). Entry to public pools is ~1,000 ISK and includes hot tubs and steam rooms. A beloved local experience much cheaper than the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aurora hunt from the beachfront near the resort. Pack warm drinks in a thermos. Download the Veður app and the My Aurora Forecast app for real-time KP index updates. Stay out until 22:00 if conditions are promising.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort — oatmeal with honey and raisins ~300 ISK
meals.lunch: Self-catered at resort — Bónus bread, cheese, and cold cuts ~600 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort — hearty vegetable and lentil soup ~700 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Midpoint rest day is important on a 13-day trip. Use this time to charge camera batteries, back up photos, and review the remaining itinerary. Public geothermal pools are a truly authentic Icelandic experience — locals use them daily.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget South Coast day tour (~10,000–12,000 ISK for a group tour). First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall — a stunning 60m cascade you can walk behind (free, though icy in January — crampons recommended). Nearby Gljúfrabúi hidden waterfall is also worth the short hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most powerful and photogenic falls (free entry). Then drive to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík — dramatic basalt columns, sea stacks, and crashing North Atlantic waves. Never turn your back on the ocean here — sneaker waves are extremely dangerous.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavík/resort by ~19:00. The South Coast drive offers excellent aurora viewing on clear nights. Check the forecast and scan the sky on the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort before early departure — bread and peanut butter ~300 ISK
meals.lunch: Pack Bónus lunch for the tour ~700 ISK. Alternatively, the Skógafoss café offers affordable soup (~1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort — rice with canned salmon and vegetables ~900 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Crampons/ice cleats are strongly recommended for Seljalandsfoss in January — the path behind the waterfall is extremely icy. Many tour companies provide them or you can buy cheap ones at Bónus/Krónan. Reynisfjara beach is beautiful but genuinely dangerous — heed all warning signs.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget Snæfellsnes Peninsula day tour (~10,000–13,000 ISK) or rent a car. Visit Kirkjufell mountain and Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most photographed landscapes and a Game of Thrones filming location. The winter light and potential snow make it spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Snæfellsjökull National Park — the glacier-capped volcano that inspired Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Visit the dramatic lava fields at Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach and the Londrangar basalt sea stacks (all free). Stop at Arnarstapi for coastal arch views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort (~20:00). The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is far from city lights — excellent aurora viewing on the return drive if skies are clear. Keep eyes on the northern horizon.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort — eggs and skyr ~400 ISK
meals.lunch: Pack Bónus lunch for the tour ~700 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort — lamb soup from packet with bread ~800 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is about 2.5 hours from Reykjavík — a long but incredibly rewarding day. The peninsula is sometimes called 'Iceland in miniature' due to its diverse landscapes. January conditions can be icy — the tour driver/guide will manage road safety.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Perlan museum in Reykjavík (~2,900 ISK) — built on five hot water storage tanks, it features a planetarium, northern lights show, and Iceland nature exhibitions. The rooftop observation deck offers panoramic views of Reykjavík and the surrounding mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Öskjuhlíð forest and down to Nauthólsvík geothermal beach — a man-made geothermal lagoon on the coast of Reykjavík where warm water is pumped into the sea (free or small fee ~700 ISK in winter). A local alternative to the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated northern lights hunt. Book a budget Northern Lights boat tour from the Old Harbour (~6,000–8,000 ISK) — sailing out to sea eliminates light pollution and cloud cover near the coast. Alternatively, join a budget bus aurora tour. Tonight is specifically reserved for the best aurora chance of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort — granola and skyr ~400 ISK
meals.lunch: Reykjavík: Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — traditional Icelandic rye bread soup bowl ~1,800 ISK (a budget splurge worth it)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort — pasta carbonara ~700 ISK (early dinner before the aurora tour)

day_by_day.notes: The Perlan northern lights planetarium show is a good backup if real aurora conditions are poor. Northern lights boat tours are often rescheduled if weather is bad — operators typically offer rebooking. Dress in your absolute warmest layers for the boat tour.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Þingvellir National Park independently for a deeper exploration (take a budget tour or rent a car ~5,000 ISK). Walk the Almannagjá rift canyon trail — free and stunning in winter. Visit the Öxará River and the historic site of the world's first parliament (Alþingi, 930 AD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the nearby Kerið volcanic crater lake (~400 ISK entry) — a stunning red and ochre caldera with a vivid blue-green lake at the bottom. In January the crater rim may be snow-covered, making it even more dramatic. Return toward the resort via the south.
day_by_day.evening: Aurora watch from the Þingvellir area if you have a rental car — one of Iceland's best dark sky locations (Bortle Class 3). Alternatively return to the resort beachfront for aurora scanning.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort — toast with Icelandic butter and jam ~300 ISK
meals.lunch: Pack Bónus lunch for the day ~700 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort — baked potato with tuna and salad ~800 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Þingvellir is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Iceland's most significant cultural and geological locations. The Silfra fissure (snorkeling/diving between tectonic plates) is available but expensive (~20,000 ISK) — skip for budget travelers. The Kerið crater is a short detour from the Golden Circle route.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — morning at leisure. Take a slow walk along the beachfront near the Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy the last glimpses of the dramatic Icelandic winter coastline. Pack non-essentials and begin organizing luggage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavík for final souvenir shopping. Visit the Kolaportið flea market (if weekend) or browse Laugavegur street for budget souvenirs — Icelandic wool products, lava salt, and skyr are popular. Visit the Sun Voyager (Sólfar) sculpture on the waterfront — free and iconic.
day_by_day.evening: Final northern lights attempt — head to the darkest accessible spot near the resort or take a short drive from the city. Set an alarm for 23:00–02:00 for the best aurora window. Celebrate the trip with a small splurge at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort — full Icelandic-style breakfast with skyr, bread, eggs ~600 ISK
meals.lunch: Reykjavík: Hlemmur Mathöll food hall — try something new ~1,500–2,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Splurge dinner: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) at the Old Harbour — famous lobster soup for ~2,500 ISK. One of Reykjavík's best budget seafood spots

day_by_day.notes: Sægreifinn's lobster soup is legendary and surprisingly affordable — a perfect final dinner splurge. For souvenirs, Bónus and Krónan sell Icelandic food products cheaply. Avoid tourist shops on Laugavegur for non-food items — they are significantly overpriced.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a last self-catered breakfast. Transfer to Keflavík International Airport via Flybus (~3,000 ISK, book in advance). Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before departure for international flights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure day — airport time. Browse duty-free for last-minute Icelandic souvenirs (Icelandic spirits, chocolate, and skyr powder are popular). Duty-free prices are often better than city shops.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland. Reflect on 13 incredible days of northern lights, hot springs, waterfalls, and volcanic landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast at resort — use up remaining Bónus supplies ~400 ISK
meals.lunch: Airport café or pack remaining snacks from the resort
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport food

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 — confirm with the resort. The Flybus can be booked to depart from the hotel or a nearby stop. Reconfirm your return flight details the evening before. January flights can occasionally be delayed due to weather — build buffer time. Keep all receipts for VAT refund claims (minimum purchase ~6,000 ISK per receipt at eligible stores — collect your refund at the airport).

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snacks
meals.dinner: Light snack at the airport or hotel – grab something from the hotel bar or a vending option upon late arrival

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Pre-arrange airport transfer before departure to avoid delays on arrival. January nights are long and cold – dress in warm layers immediately upon landing.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Take time to orient yourself, check the northern lights forecast app (Vedur.is), and plan the week ahead. Walk along the beachfront near the resort if weather permits – dramatic January coastal scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the world-famous Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (pre-book in advance). Soak in the milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and sulfur minerals. Enjoy in-water treatments, silica mud masks, and the serene steaming pools. The lagoon is very close to Keflavík airport, making it ideal for a jet-lag recovery soak.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and freshen up. Head out for your first Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep – guides will drive you away from light pollution into the Icelandic wilderness for the best aurora viewing conditions. January offers some of the longest dark windows of the year.

meals.breakfast: Hotel buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – included or à la carte
meals.lunch: LAVA Restaurant inside Blue Lagoon (mid-range option) or pack a light snack from a nearby Netto or Krónan grocery store
meals.dinner: Warm soup or lamb stew at a local restaurant near the resort, or hotel dining upon return from the northern lights tour

day_by_day.notes: Book the Blue Lagoon well in advance – slots sell out quickly. Northern lights tours typically depart around 21:00–22:00 and last 3–4 hours. Dress in full thermal layers, waterproof jacket, gloves, and hat for the evening tour.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after late northern lights tour. Enjoy a slow breakfast at the hotel. Browse local visitor information and pick up a Reykjavík City Card if planning city exploration later in the week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a bus into Reykjavík (about 45 minutes from the Reykjanes Peninsula area). Join the Reykjavík Food & Culture Walking Tour – sample traditional Icelandic cuisine including skyr, lamb soup, fermented shark (hákarl), and fresh seafood while exploring landmarks like Hallgrímskirkja church, Harpa Concert Hall, and the colorful old harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavík's Laugavegur street – browse boutique shops and galleries. Dinner in the city before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Included tastings during the Food & Culture Walking Tour
meals.dinner: Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja – traditional Icelandic dishes at mid-range prices (try the lamb meat soup and rye bread ice cream)

day_by_day.notes: The walking tour lasts approximately 3 hours. Wear comfortable waterproof boots as January streets can be icy. Sunset in Iceland in January is around 11:30–12:00, so afternoon light is very limited – embrace the moody blue-hour atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Golden Circle Day – Depart early (8:00 AM) to maximize limited daylight. First stop: Þingvellir (Thingvellir) National Park – walk the rift valley between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. A UNESCO World Heritage Site with dramatic geological formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle: Visit the Geysir Geothermal Area to watch Strokkur erupt every 5–10 minutes. Then drive to the majestic Gullfoss waterfall – partially frozen in January, creating spectacular icy formations. Grab a warm meal at the Gullfoss Café.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the resort. If aurora forecast is favorable (KP index 3+), pull over at a dark rural spot or join another guided Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep for a second chance at aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or packed snacks to go
meals.lunch: Gullfoss Café – hearty lamb soup and Icelandic pastries (mid-range, around 2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or a nearby grill house – try Icelandic lamb chops or fish of the day

day_by_day.notes: Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip. Rent a car or join a guided Golden Circle day tour from Reykjavík. Roads can be icy – check road.is before departure. Bring a thermos of hot tea or coffee.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the hotel. Visit the resort's hot spring or pool facilities if available. Catch up on rest and review photos from previous days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir – Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this natural hot spring offers an authentic and affordable geothermal bathing experience surrounded by geysers and steam vents. Water temperature is a constant 38–40°C.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the quiet Flúðir village area before heading back. Stop at a local grocery store (Krónan or Bónus) to stock up on snacks and drinks. Evening aurora watch from the hotel grounds or nearby dark coastal area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch or stop at a roadside petrol station café (Orkan or N1) for a hot dog – Iceland's iconic pylsur is a must-try
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the hotel room using groceries, or hotel restaurant – grilled fish with Icelandic potatoes

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon entry is around 2,800 ISK (much more affordable than Blue Lagoon). Bring a swimsuit, towel, and flip-flops. The drive from Reykjanes Peninsula to Flúðir is about 1.5 hours each way – plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: South Coast adventure begins. Drive east along the South Coast. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall – walk behind the curtain of falling water (may be icy in January, so exercise caution). Then visit nearby Skógafoss waterfall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík. Marvel at the dramatic basalt column formations (Reynisdrangar sea stacks) and powerful Atlantic waves. Visit the charming village of Vík í Mýrdal and its iconic hillside church.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back west. Stop for dinner in Selfoss town. Check aurora forecast – if favorable, find a dark pull-off on the drive home for aurora spotting.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Skál! in Vík or the Black Beach Restaurant near Reynisfjara – lamb burger or fish and chips (mid-range)
meals.dinner: Kaffi Krús in Selfoss – cozy atmosphere, excellent lamb dishes and Icelandic fish stew

day_by_day.notes: NEVER turn your back on the ocean at Reynisfjara – sneaker waves are extremely dangerous. Roads east of Vík can close in winter storms – check road.is before heading out. This is a long driving day (~350 km round trip).

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day. Sleep in and enjoy a long hotel breakfast. Take a gentle walk along the beachfront near the resort. Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula's unique volcanic landscape nearby – visit the Bridge Between Continents (a small footbridge over the tectonic rift).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjanes Lighthouse (Valahnúkamöl) and the dramatic coastal cliffs at Reykjanestá – the most southwesterly point of Iceland. Explore the nearby geothermal fields at Gunnuhver, where steaming mud pools and fumaroles create an otherworldly landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hotel. Enjoy a spa treatment or hot tub soak if available at Aegean Bliss Resort. Early dinner and an early night to recharge.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel buffet breakfast
meals.lunch: Café or bakery in Grindavík town – fresh pastries and Icelandic coffee
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant – splurge slightly on a nice seafood platter or Icelandic lamb rack as a mid-trip treat

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is geologically very active – you may see steam rising from the ground in multiple locations. This is a great low-key day to recharge mid-trip. Keep an eye on aurora forecasts for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Snæfellsnes Peninsula day trip (long but spectacular). Depart by 7:00 AM. Drive north to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula – home of the famous Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano (Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth'). Stop at Kirkjufell mountain and its waterfall – one of Iceland's most photographed landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Snæfellsjökull National Park – walk among lava fields, dramatic sea cliffs, and black sand beaches. Visit the Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach and the ruins of a shipwreck. Stop at the charming fishing village of Arnarstapi.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back south. This is a very long day – arrive back at the resort by 21:00–22:00. If aurora activity is high, stop at a dark spot on the way home.

meals.breakfast: Very early hotel breakfast or packed food to go
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from grocery store or stop at a petrol station café en route
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Stykkishólmur town on the peninsula (Narfeyrarstofa – excellent seafood) or dinner back at the hotel upon return

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is approximately 200 km from Reykjavík – budget 3 hours driving each way. This is a full and demanding day. Consider joining a guided day tour to avoid driving fatigue. Roads on the peninsula can be challenging in January.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning to recover from the Snæfellsnes day trip. Hotel breakfast and a slow start. Browse local shops near the resort or relax with a book.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavík for an afternoon of culture. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) to learn about Viking history and Icelandic heritage. Then walk to the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and take the elevator to the top for panoramic city views (limited daylight but still dramatic).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Reykjavík's Friday night atmosphere on Laugavegur. Browse the weekend flea market at Kolaportið (closes at 17:00 – visit before dinner). Dinner in the city and a leisurely return to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Sandholt Bakery on Laugavegur – excellent sourdough sandwiches, pastries, and coffee (Icelandic institution)
meals.dinner: Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) – upscale but worth the splurge for premium Icelandic ingredients; or Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) for affordable lobster soup

day_by_day.notes: National Museum admission is around 2,500 ISK. Hallgrímskirkja tower ticket is about 1,000 ISK. Kolaportið flea market is open Saturday–Sunday 11:00–17:00. Great place to find affordable Icelandic wool products and local snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike & Natural Pool – depart early for this spectacular highland experience. Trek through Iceland's rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Fjallabak Nature Reserve. Note: access may be limited in deep winter – confirm with tour operator that this route is accessible in January (some operators run snowmobile or super jeep access).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the Landmannalaugar natural hot spring pool. Soak in the geothermal pool surrounded by snow-dusted multicolored mountains – a truly magical contrast of hot water and winter wilderness. Explore the area's steaming fumaroles and obsidian lava fields.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to the resort (guided tour returns you to the meeting point). Warm up with a hot meal and early rest.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch (sandwiches, energy bars, thermos of soup) – no restaurants in the highland area
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or nearby restaurant – hearty lamb stew or fish pie to warm up after a cold outdoor day

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar in January REQUIRES a guided super jeep tour – the F-roads are impassable without a specialized vehicle. Book well in advance. Bring a swimsuit under your thermals, a dry bag, extra warm layers, and waterproof everything. This is one of the most unique experiences in Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Slow morning at the hotel. Enjoy breakfast and begin packing non-essential items. Take a final walk along the beachfront – soak in the dramatic January coastal atmosphere of Iceland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Blue Lagoon for a second relaxing soak – this time without the rush of Day 2. Treat yourself to a silica mud mask ritual and algae mask add-on. A perfect way to unwind before the final days of the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep – book this as your last dedicated aurora chase of the trip. With 13 days in Iceland in January, you have excellent odds of seeing the aurora at least once. Tonight, make it special.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: LAVA Restaurant at Blue Lagoon – try the Icelandic langoustine bisque
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the hotel or a nearby Grindavík restaurant before the evening aurora tour

day_by_day.notes: Re-booking the Blue Lagoon for a second visit is worthwhile for relaxation purposes. If you already saw the northern lights earlier in the trip, this evening tour is still a wonderful experience – no two aurora displays are alike.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day in Iceland. Check out of the resort or arrange late checkout. Drive or take a bus into Reykjavík for final souvenir shopping on Laugavegur. Look for Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa), local chocolate, skyr, and volcanic salt.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Harpa Concert Hall for a self-guided tour of its stunning geometric glass architecture. Walk along the old harbor (Grandi area) and visit the Whales of Iceland exhibition or the Icelandic Phallological Museum for something unique. Final coffee at a Reykjavík café.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Reykjavík. Return to the resort or stay near the airport area for an easy morning departure.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – last one, enjoy it!
meals.lunch: Messinn restaurant in Reykjavík – famous for their cast-iron pan fish dishes, excellent value
meals.dinner: Fiskmarkaðurinn (The Fish Market) – a special farewell dinner featuring creative Icelandic seafood with Asian influences; or Snaps Bistro for a more casual but excellent French-Icelandic bistro experience

day_by_day.notes: If you haven't purchased souvenirs yet, Laugavegur and Skólavörðustígur streets have the best selection. Avoid overpriced airport shops. Pack an extra bag for any wool items purchased. Confirm flight details and transfer timing for tomorrow morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Wake up early, enjoy one last hotel breakfast. Check out and arrange transfer to Keflavík International Airport (approximately 45 minutes from the Reykjanes Peninsula area). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of northern lights, hot springs, volcanic landscapes, and Icelandic culture.
day_by_day.evening: In transit home

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or airport café at Keflavík (Fljúgandi Fiskar or airport restaurants)
meals.lunch: Airport dining or in-flight meal
meals.dinner: In-flight or at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Keflavík Airport has decent dining and shopping options airside. Currency exchange rates are poor at airports – spend remaining ISK on food, drinks, or duty-free Icelandic spirits (Brennivín). Leave a small buffer of ISK for any last-minute expenses.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution for the best chance of witnessing the aurora borealis. Expert guides track solar activity and cloud cover to maximize your viewing experience, often venturing to remote highland areas.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & South Iceland highlands, departing from Reykjavik

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and sulfur minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and a swim-up bar serving Icelandic refreshments. Book the Comfort package for the full experience including towel and one drink.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (sunset or after dark for a magical atmosphere)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits amid bubbling hot springs and small geysers in a stunning rural landscape. A truly local and intimate experience.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and cultural landmarks on a guided walking tour. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, and Icelandic hot dogs. Visit the iconic Hallgrimskirkja church, the colorful old harbor, and local artisan shops.
experiences.location: 101 Reykjavik city center & Old Harbor district

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike & Natural Pool
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's stunning rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Fjallabak Nature Reserve and reward yourself with a soak in a natural geothermal hot spring river. The hike offers surreal landscapes of obsidian lava fields, steaming vents, and vivid mineral-streaked mountains unlike anywhere else on Earth.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer (pre-arranged Mercedes V-Class or similar) whisks you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, enjoy a late welcome amenity – warm Icelandic lamb soup and a glass of Champagne prepared by the resort – and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: In-flight or airport lounge
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome amenity at Aegean Bliss Resort – warm Icelandic lamb soup, artisan bread, and Champagne courtesy of the resort

day_by_day.notes: Nothing is scheduled before arrival. Confirm private airport transfer 48 hours in advance. Request early check-in amenities and a wake-up call preference for Day 2. Keep luggage light for easy evening check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the resort's signature restaurant overlooking the beachfront. Take a gentle stroll along the black-sand shoreline to acclimate to Iceland's dramatic winter landscape and crisp Arctic air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa – Just a short luxury transfer from the resort (approx. 15–20 minutes), indulge in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters. Book the premium 'Retreat' package which includes an in-water floating massage, silica mud mask, algae mask, access to the exclusive Retreat Spa, and a private changing suite. Spend 3–4 hours unwinding in the mineral-rich 38–40°C waters.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at Lava Restaurant inside the Blue Lagoon complex, perched dramatically over the lava field with floor-to-ceiling windows. Enjoy a tasting menu featuring Icelandic langoustine, Arctic char, and skyr-based desserts. Return to the resort via private transfer and check for northern lights activity from your beachfront suite terrace.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort – Full Icelandic gourmet breakfast buffet with smoked salmon, skyr, rye bread, and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Retreat Lounge – Included light bites: Icelandic flatbread, smoked trout, and sparkling water served in-water or at the lounge
meals.dinner: Lava Restaurant at Blue Lagoon – Multi-course tasting menu with wine pairing (approx. ISK 25,000–35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Blue Lagoon Retreat package well in advance as slots sell out weeks ahead, especially in January. Bring a hair tie and consider the in-water hair conditioner treatment to protect hair from the mineral-rich water.

day_by_day.morning: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour – Private guided luxury version of this iconic tour. Depart from the resort via private car to central Reykjavik (approx. 45 minutes). Explore Hallgrímskirkja church, the colorful old harbor district, and Laugavegur street. Sample traditional Icelandic delicacies including hákarl (fermented shark), pylsur (Icelandic hot dog from Bæjarins Beztu), skyr parfait, and freshly baked kleinur doughnuts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the cultural exploration with a private visit to the Harpa Concert Hall and the National Museum of Iceland. Browse high-end Icelandic design boutiques along Skólavörðustígur for luxury woolens, hand-crafted jewelry, and artisan gifts. Visit the Kolaportið flea market for authentic local character.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep – After dinner, join an elite small-group (or fully private) Super Jeep northern lights expedition departing from Reykjavik. Expert guides use real-time aurora forecasting apps and satellite data to drive away from light pollution into the Reykjanes Peninsula or Þingvellir National Park. Enjoy hot chocolate and Icelandic spirits under the stars while waiting for the aurora to dance.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort – À la carte breakfast with Icelandic pancakes, smoked lamb, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Messinn Restaurant, Reykjavik – Renowned for its cast-iron skillets of fresh Icelandic fish; try the pan-fried Arctic char or langoustine skillet
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavik – Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant. Nordic New Wave cuisine with a 7-course tasting menu featuring hyper-local, foraged Icelandic ingredients and a curated Icelandic wine/spirits pairing

day_by_day.notes: Northern lights tours typically depart 21:00–22:00 and return by 01:00–02:00. Dress in multiple thermal layers; the resort concierge can provide or rent premium Arctic outerwear. January offers some of the longest darkness windows of the year – excellent aurora conditions if skies are clear.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after the late northern lights tour. Sleep in, then enjoy a private in-suite breakfast delivered by the resort. Spend the morning in the resort's spa facilities – sauna, steam room, and hot tub – to recharge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Golden Circle Luxury Tour – Depart by private luxury 4WD for Iceland's iconic Golden Circle. Visit Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site, where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet), the geothermal Geysir area to witness Strokkur erupting every 5–10 minutes, and the majestic Gullfoss waterfall, spectacular even in its partially frozen January state.
day_by_day.evening: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak – Conclude the Golden Circle loop with a visit to the Secret Lagoon in Flúðir, Iceland's oldest natural hot spring pool dating to 1891. Far more intimate and atmospheric than the Blue Lagoon, with natural geothermal pools, steaming geysers, and a rustic wooden changing facility. Soak under the winter sky and watch for northern lights on the drive back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: In-suite gourmet breakfast service at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant, Reykholt – Dine inside a working geothermal tomato greenhouse. Famous for its tomato-based menu: tomato soup, tomato bruschetta, and tomato beer, with fresh bread baked on-site
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant – Enjoy a leisurely dinner back at the resort; request the chef's tasting menu featuring the catch of the day and Icelandic lamb with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle in January means short daylight hours (approximately 5–6 hours of light). Depart by 10:30 to maximize daylight at Þingvellir and Geysir. Roads are generally well-maintained but confirm conditions with the resort concierge each morning.

day_by_day.morning: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike & Natural Pool – Depart early by private Super Jeep (mandatory for F-road access) for the Fjallabak Nature Reserve. The journey itself is spectacular, crossing highland roads and frozen rivers. Arrive at Landmannalaugar and trek through the surreal rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains, obsidian lava fields, and steaming fumaroles. The landscape is otherworldly in winter with snow dusting the multicolored peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Landmannalaugar experience by soaking in the natural geothermal hot spring pool where a hot stream meets a cold glacial river, allowing you to find your perfect temperature. Enjoy packed gourmet picnic provisions prepared by the resort. Explore the surrounding area on shorter winter-accessible trails with your guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to the resort (approximately 3–4 hours). Freshen up and enjoy a quiet, indulgent evening at the resort. Request a private northern lights wake-up call service from the resort – they will call your room if the aurora becomes visible during the night.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort – Early hearty breakfast with porridge, eggs, smoked fish, and strong Icelandic coffee to fuel the highland adventure
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed picnic prepared by the resort chef – artisan sandwiches with Icelandic lamb and cheese, thermos of hot soup, fresh fruit, and Icelandic chocolate
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort – Intimate in-suite dinner or restaurant dining; try the slow-roasted Icelandic lamb shank with root vegetables and a bottle of Burgundy

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar in January requires an experienced Super Jeep driver and guide. Conditions can be challenging; the trip may need to be rescheduled if highland roads are closed due to weather. Always check road conditions at road.is. Bring a swimsuit, towel, and waterproof changing robe for the hot spring soak.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at the resort. Enjoy the resort's beachfront setting – take a dramatic winter walk along the volcanic shoreline, watch waves crash against the black lava rocks, and spot local birdlife. Visit the resort's wellness center for a signature Icelandic body treatment using geothermal minerals and Arctic botanicals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private South Coast Adventure – Depart by luxury 4WD for Iceland's legendary South Coast. Visit the stunning Seljalandsfoss waterfall (walk behind the cascade in winter with crampons provided by your guide), Skógafoss waterfall with its rainbow mist, and the black-sand beach of Reynisfjara with its dramatic basalt column formations and powerful Atlantic surf.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep – Second attempt at the aurora, this time heading east along the South Coast away from Reykjavik's light pollution. The flat, open landscape of the South Coast offers unobstructed 360-degree sky views – ideal aurora-watching conditions. Your guide will position the jeep for optimal photography. Hot drinks and local spirits provided.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort – Full breakfast with skyr waffles, fresh berries, and Icelandic flat bread with smoked salmon
meals.lunch: Skál! at Hlemmur Food Hall, Reykjavik (en route) – Upscale food hall experience; try the Icelandic fish tacos and craft local beers
meals.dinner: Strondin Bistro & Bar, Vík – Cozy restaurant in the charming village of Vík; known for fresh local seafood and Icelandic lamb with stunning views of Reynisfjara beach

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara beach has extremely dangerous sneaker waves – always stay well back from the waterline and follow your guide's instructions. Crampons are essential for Seljalandsfoss in January. The South Coast drive is approximately 2.5 hours from the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip leisure and spa day. Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning. Book a 90-minute couples' or solo Icelandic Hot Stone Massage at the resort spa, incorporating volcanic basalt stones and geothermal mineral oils. Spend time in the resort's geothermal outdoor hot tub overlooking the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Snæfellsnes Peninsula Day Tour – Depart by luxury 4WD for the mystical Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approx. 2 hours from the resort), home to the glacier-capped Snæfellsjökull volcano immortalized in Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Centre of the Earth.' Visit Kirkjufell mountain (Iceland's most photographed peak), Arnarstapi coastal cliffs with their dramatic sea arches, and the charming fishing village of Grundarfjörður.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a celebratory mid-trip dinner. Request the resort's private chef's table experience – a personalized 8-course tasting menu in an intimate setting with the chef presenting each course and explaining the Icelandic provenance of every ingredient. Wine sommelier pairing included.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort – Leisurely breakfast in bed with fresh pastries, fruit platter, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Bjargarsteinn Mathús, Grundarfjörður – A celebrated local restaurant on the Snæfellsnes Peninsula; known for incredibly fresh langoustine soup and pan-seared cod
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort Private Chef's Table – 8-course personalized tasting menu with Icelandic ingredients and premium wine/spirits pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is approximately 2–2.5 hours from the resort. Depart by 11:00 to maximize the limited winter daylight. Kirkjufell with its surrounding waterfalls is especially magical in winter with ice formations and potential northern lights backdrop in the evening sky.

day_by_day.morning: Private Reykjanes Peninsula Geothermal Exploration – The Reykjanes Peninsula, just minutes from the resort, is one of the most geologically active areas on Earth. Take a private guided walk through the Gunnuhver hot spring area (Iceland's largest hot mud pool), the Bridge Between Continents (walk between the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates), and the Reykjanesviti lighthouse perched on dramatic lava cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Blue Lagoon for a second visit – this time booking the exclusive 'Signature' in-water massage treatment and the Lava Restaurant for a private dining experience. Alternatively, explore the Keflavík area and visit the Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark visitor center to understand the volcanic forces shaping Iceland.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset (around 16:30 in January) cocktail hour on the resort terrace with a private mixologist preparing Icelandic-inspired cocktails using local spirits like Brennivín (Icelandic schnapps) and crowberry liqueur. Then enjoy dinner at the resort's premium restaurant with a focus on the freshest Icelandic seafood.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort – Scandinavian-style cold buffet with cured fish, pickled vegetables, artisan cheeses, and rye crispbread
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant at Blue Lagoon – À la carte lunch with Icelandic lobster bisque, smoked duck salad, and house-baked sourdough
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort – Seafood-focused tasting menu: Icelandic langoustine, pan-seared halibut, and a skyr cheesecake finale with a curated Chablis and white Burgundy pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is highly accessible from the resort – ideal for a relaxed day without long drives. Note that volcanic activity in the Reykjanes area has been ongoing; your guide will confirm which areas are safe to visit and may offer the exciting possibility of viewing recent lava fields.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Hiking & Ice Cave Exploration – Depart early by luxury 4WD for Sólheimajökull glacier (approx. 2 hours). Join a private guided glacier hike with premium crampons, ice axes, and harnesses provided. Walk across the ancient blue ice, explore crevasses, and witness the dramatic contrast of black volcanic ash layers within the glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to a nearby natural ice cave (location varies by year as caves form and change seasonally – your guide will know the best active caves). These ethereal blue crystal caverns inside glaciers are among Iceland's most extraordinary natural wonders, accessible only in winter when the ice is stable. Photography opportunities are exceptional.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey with a stop at the village of Hveragerði – a geothermal town where residents grow tropical fruits in greenhouse gardens heated by the earth. Visit a local greenhouse bakery for fresh geothermally-baked rye bread straight from the ground. Return to the resort for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort – High-energy pre-adventure breakfast: oatmeal with Icelandic honey, scrambled eggs with smoked salmon, and energy bars
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic from the resort – hot thermos of lamb and vegetable soup, gourmet sandwiches, Icelandic chocolate, and warm drinks
meals.dinner: Rauða Húsið (The Red House), Eyrarbakki – A charming historic restaurant in a 19th-century red house near the south coast; famous for its exceptional lobster soup and Icelandic fish dishes in an intimate, candlelit setting

day_by_day.notes: Ice cave access depends entirely on safety conditions assessed by guides on the day. Natural ice caves are only accessible November–March. All glacier and ice cave equipment is provided by the guide company; wear warm, waterproof base layers. This is a physically active day – moderate fitness required.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning and resort indulgence. Take a sunrise walk (around 11:00 in January) along the Reykjanes beachfront as the winter light paints the sky in shades of pink and gold. Enjoy a long brunch at the resort and spend time reading, journaling, or simply absorbing the dramatic Icelandic coastal scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Whale Watching & Coastal Boat Tour – From the nearby Reykjavík Old Harbor, board a premium luxury yacht for a private whale watching excursion. January offers sightings of humpback whales, minke whales, and white-beaked dolphins in Faxaflói Bay. Blankets, hot drinks, and binoculars provided on board. The dramatic backdrop of Mount Esja and the Reykjanes Peninsula makes for extraordinary photography.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep – Third aurora expedition, this time heading north toward Þingvellir National Park for a different landscape. Your guide will have been monitoring solar activity throughout the trip and will optimize this final dedicated aurora hunt. Celebrate any sightings with Icelandic Champagne under the dancing lights.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort – Leisurely brunch: eggs Benedict with smoked Icelandic lamb, fresh fruit, pastries, and Bloody Mary or fresh juice
meals.lunch: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron), Reykjavík Old Harbor – A legendary Reykjavík institution; famous for its lobster soup and grilled fish skewers served in a rustic harbor shack atmosphere – a beloved local contrast to fine dining
meals.dinner: Grillið Restaurant, Radisson Blu Saga Hotel, Reykjavík – Rooftop fine dining with panoramic city views; renowned for its premium Icelandic beef, rack of lamb, and exceptional wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching in January can be weather-dependent; the tour operator will advise on sea conditions. The private yacht option provides significantly more comfort and exclusivity than group tours. Dress in full Arctic outerwear for the boat – wind chill on the water is intense.

day_by_day.morning: Private Waterfalls & Hidden Gems Tour – Explore lesser-known but spectacular waterfalls near the resort: Öxará River at Þingvellir, the hidden Gjáin valley (a magical moss-covered gorge with multiple cascades), and Háifoss, one of Iceland's tallest waterfalls. Your private guide will take you off the tourist trail to experience Iceland's raw natural beauty without the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the geothermal area of Haukadalur Valley – beyond the famous Geysir, explore the quieter thermal pools, mud pots, and steaming vents that stretch across the landscape. Stop at the Geysir Center for a warm drink and browse the quality gift shop for premium Icelandic woolens and design items.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at the resort bar, then a special premium farewell dinner at the resort's finest dining room. Work with the sommelier in advance to select a special bottle of wine to mark the occasion. Reflect on the journey over an indulgent multi-course meal.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort – Full Icelandic breakfast with all favorites: smoked fish, skyr, fresh bread, eggs, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Geysir Center Restaurant – Warm and hearty Icelandic lamb soup with fresh bread; simple but perfect after a cold morning outdoors
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort Signature Restaurant – Premium farewell dinner: 6-course tasting menu with Icelandic caviar amuse-bouche, langoustine bisque, slow-cooked lamb, artisan cheese selection, and a skyr soufflé; paired with a curated wine journey

day_by_day.notes: Gjáin Valley may have limited accessibility in January due to snow – confirm with your guide the morning of the tour. This day is designed as a more relaxed exploration day before the final full days of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final Reykjavík Luxury Shopping & Cultural Morning – Private car to Reykjavík for a final morning of premium shopping and cultural experiences. Visit the flagship stores of Icelandic designers: 66°North (premium outdoor wear), Farmers & Friends (Icelandic wool and design), and Aurum (fine Icelandic jewelry). Visit the stunning Perlan museum for an immersive exhibition on Icelandic nature, glaciers, and the northern lights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Secret Lagoon Return Visit – For a final geothermal soak, revisit the Secret Lagoon in Flúðir for a peaceful, unhurried afternoon in the natural hot spring. With fewer tourists than the Blue Lagoon and a deeply authentic atmosphere, this is the perfect way to spend your final full afternoon in Iceland – floating in warm geothermal water surrounded by steam and silence.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for final packing. Enjoy a private farewell experience arranged by the resort – perhaps a bonfire on the beach with Icelandic spirits and stargazing, or a private in-suite dessert and Champagne service. Keep eyes on the northern sky for one final aurora opportunity.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort – Special farewell breakfast with the chef's selection of Icelandic morning favorites
meals.lunch: Café Loki, Reykjavík – Directly opposite Hallgrímskirkja; a beloved traditional Icelandic café serving rye bread ice cream, smoked lamb, and traditional meat soup in a cozy setting
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort – Relaxed à la carte final dinner; choose your favorites from the menu, paired with a farewell glass of Icelandic craft beer or wine

day_by_day.notes: Allow time for final packing and organizing luggage for the early departure the following morning. Confirm private airport transfer time with the resort concierge. Request a packed breakfast or early morning coffee service for Day 13 if departure is very early.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Wake up for a last look at the dramatic Reykjanes beachfront at dawn (sunrise approximately 11:00 in January, so pre-departure light will be limited but atmospheric). Enjoy a final breakfast at the resort or in-suite if departing early. Check out and depart via pre-arranged private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight departure time, utilize the Keflavík Airport premium lounge facilities. Consider a final quick stop at the Blue Lagoon Spa (which has a dedicated airport proximity package) for a farewell soak before your flight – the Blue Lagoon is literally 5 minutes from the airport, making it the world's most convenient pre-flight luxury spa experience.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Carry memories of aurora-lit skies, geothermal waters, volcanic landscapes, and world-class Icelandic cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort – Final in-suite or restaurant breakfast; request a packed gourmet breakfast box if departing before the restaurant opens
meals.lunch: Keflavík Airport Premium Lounge or Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant (if time permits for a final pre-flight visit)
meals.dinner: In-flight

day_by_day.notes: Confirm exact checkout time and transfer schedule with the resort the evening before. Keflavík Airport is approximately 15–20 minutes from the resort – a significant advantage of the resort's location. Allow extra time for check-in during peak winter travel season. Duty-free at Keflavík offers excellent Icelandic spirits (Brennivín, Flóki Whisky), premium smoked fish, and Icelandic chocolates as farewell gifts.
